blocks.text: To manufacture sulfuric acid, sulfur trioxide is produced from SO2 and O2 in a reversible process, 2SO2(g) + O2(g) giving 2SO3(g), delta H = -97.9 kJ per mol. By Le Chatelier's principle high pressure and low temperature are the conditions for a better yield of SO3. At low temperature the equilibrium constant for SO3 formation is large but equilibrium is reached very slowly; as the temperature rises the rate increases but the yield of SO3 drops. Table 8.2 shows the position at 1 atmosphere.

blocks.caption: Effect of temperature on the SO3 equilibrium at 1 atm (Table 8.2)

blocks.text: For the best yield of SO3 within a reasonable time, a mixture of SO2(g) and O2(g) (as air) at one atmosphere is passed over a solid catalyst such as V2O5. Because the reaction is exothermic the temperature of the gas rises to 600 degrees C, so the equilibrium mixture is recycled at the lower temperature of 400 to 500 degrees C to increase the yield of SO3(g).

blocks.prompt: Using Table 8.2, explain why the contact process does not simply run at 200 degrees C, where 98 per cent of the sulfur dioxide is converted.
blocks.explanation: At 200 degrees C Kc is 5500 and the equilibrium yield 98 per cent, but the reaction is far too slow to reach that equilibrium in a useful time. At 400 to 500 degrees C, with vanadium pentoxide as catalyst, the rate is high and the yield (75 to 61 per cent at equilibrium) is still good; recycling the gases at this lower temperature after the exothermic heating converts more of the remaining SO2.

items: 2SO2 + O2 giving 2SO3, exothermic (-97.9 kJ per mol): low temperature gives large Kc and high yield (98 per cent at 200 degrees C) but slowly; high temperature is fast but the yield falls (31 per cent at 700 degrees C).
Optimum: SO2 and air at 1 atm over V2O5; the gas heats to 600 degrees C, so the mixture is recycled at 400 to 500 degrees C.
